name: Somali Bariis Iskukaris
description: Bariis iskukaris, Somalia's national dish, literally means 'cooked mixed together', describing its real one-pot technique - rice, meat, and vegetables all cook in the same pot, the rice absorbing a rich meat-and-spice broth rather than being steamed separately. Real xawaash, Somalia's essential spice blend, is built from cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon together, and real raisins are a genuine, traditional addition for sweetness - the dish is traditionally eaten by hand, using a slice of banana to scoop.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion over medium heat, stirring often, 15-18 minutes, until deeply golden - this real, patient browning is central to the dish's flavor.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon, and cook 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and brown, 6-7 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook until the mixture thickens and the oil separates at the edges, 4-5 minutes.
Add the rice, raisins, and broth, cover, and simmer 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Serve with a slice of banana alongside, the traditional accompaniment.

name: Somali Suqaar
description: Suqaar, small cubes of meat sautéed with onion, pepper, and xawaash, is a beloved Somali everyday dish, real technique searing the meat hot and fast to keep it tender rather than stewing it long.
steps_detailed: Sear the beef over high heat, 4-5 minutes, until well browned but still tender inside.
Add the onion, bell pepper, garlic, cumin, and coriander, and cook 5-6 minutes more.

name: Somali Xawaash Spice Blend
description: Xawaash, Somalia's essential spice blend, is the real foundation underlying countless Somali dishes - built from cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon together, this blend traces its roots to Yemeni hawaij.
steps_detailed: Toast each spice briefly in a dry pan, 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Mix together thoroughly and store in an airtight container.

name: Somali Malawah
description: Malawah, a sweet, slightly spongy pancake, is a beloved Somali breakfast, real technique letting the batter rest so it develops real bubbles before cooking.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, egg, and milk into a smooth batter.
Let rest 15 minutes.
Cook in a lightly oiled pan, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden.

name: Somali Sabaayad
description: Sabaayad, a layered flatbread, reflects genuine Indian and Yemeni culinary influence, real technique coiling the dough before flattening to build real flaky layers.
steps_detailed: Work the flour with warm water and half the oil into a soft dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll thin, brush with the remaining oil, and coil before flattening again to build real layers.
Cook in a hot, dry pan, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden.

Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.
